```{r}
student_preferences_round_1_path <- "data/BA_01_Preferences_Students.csv"
n_topics <- 4
available_topic_ids <- 1:n_topics
n_topics_per_student <- 2
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)

here::i_am("main.rmd")

```

```{r}
student_preferences_round_1 <- read_csv(
  file = here(student_preferences_round_1_path)
  )

n_students <- nrow(student_preferences_round_1)


student_preferences_round_1_long <- student_preferences_round_1 |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = tidyselect::all_of(paste0("preference_", seq_len(n_topics))),
    names_to = "topic_id",
    names_prefix = "preference_",
    values_to = "rank")


# ---- Helper: coerce inputs & checks ----
validate_prefs <- function(preferences, objects) {
  req_cols <- c("student_id", "topic_id", "rank")
  if (!all(req_cols %in% names(preferences))) {
    abort("`preferences` must have columns: student_id, topic_id, rank (rank 1 = most preferred).")
  }
  preferences %>%
    mutate(
      student_id = as.character(student_id),
      topic_id = as.character(topic_id),
      rank = as.integer(rank)
    ) %>%
    filter(topic_id %in% objects) %>%
    arrange(student_id, rank)
}

# Preparations
## Create long randomized list of topic ids to use as filler.
topics_filler <- unlist(replicate(n_topics_per_student, sample(available_topic_ids), simplify = FALSE))



# Step 1 - Create Topic Pools

create_topic_pool <- function(round) {
    multiplier <- ceiling(n_students / n_topics)
    
    if(multiplier < 1) {
      message("The case that there are more topics than students is not yet supported.")
    } else if(multiplier == 1) {
      tf <- NULL
    } else {
    n_filler <- (n_topics * multiplier) %% n_students
    beginning <- ((round - 1) * n_filler) + 1
    tf <- topics_filler[beginning:(beginning + n_filler - 1)]
    }
    topic_pool <- c(rep(available_topic_ids, multiplier), tf)
  
  # sanity check
  if(length(topic_pool) != n_students) {
    message(paste0("There is something wrong with the topic pool generation for round ", round))
  }
  return(topic_pool)
}

topic_pools <- lapply(1:n_topics_per_student, function(r) create_topic_pool(r))
```


```{r}
# Step 2 - allocate topics by random serial dictatorship
allocate_by_random_serial_dictatorship <- function(
  preferences,
  topic_pools,              # list: one vector of topic_ids per round
  seed = NULL
) {
  if (!is.null(seed)) set.seed(seed)

  # Validate preferences against the union of all topics that can ever appear
  all_topic_ids <- unique(unlist(topic_pools, use.names = FALSE))
  prefs <- validate_prefs(preferences, all_topic_ids)

  student_ids <- unique(prefs$student_id)
  n_students  <- length(student_ids)
  n_rounds    <- length(topic_pools)

  # 1) Hard-fail if any round's pool size != number of students
  pool_sizes <- vapply(topic_pools, length, integer(1))
  bad_rounds <- which(pool_sizes != n_students)
  if (length(bad_rounds) > 0) {
    stop(
      "Pool size mismatch: each round must have exactly ", n_students,
      " topics (one per student). Offending rounds: ",
      paste0(sprintf("#%d (size=%d)", bad_rounds, pool_sizes[bad_rounds]), collapse = ", "),
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  # Fast lookup: each student's ordered preference list (best -> worst)
  student_id_lists <- prefs %>%
    dplyr::arrange(student_id, rank) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(student_id) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(pref_list = list(topic_id), .groups = "drop") %>%
    tibble::deframe()

  # Output: rows = students, cols = rounds
  assign_mat <- matrix(
    NA_character_, nrow = n_students, ncol = n_rounds,
    dimnames = list(student_ids, paste0("topic_", seq_len(n_rounds)))
  )

  # Track topics already assigned to each student across rounds
  assigned_by_student <- stats::setNames(vector("list", n_students), student_ids)

  # Helper: pick highest-ranked topic for sid from current round's available,
  # excluding topics the student already has in previous rounds.
  first_available_for <- function(sid, available_vec) {
    prefs_for_s <- student_id_lists[[sid]]
    if (is.null(prefs_for_s)) return(NA_character_)
    available_for_student <- setdiff(available_vec, assigned_by_student[[sid]])
    choice <- purrr::keep(prefs_for_s, ~ .x %in% available_for_student) %>%
      purrr::pluck(1, .default = NA_character_)
    choice
  }

  # 2) Process each round independently with a fresh random order
  for (r in seq_len(n_rounds)) {
    available <- topic_pools[[r]]
    order_vec <- sample(student_ids, n_students)  # new random order each round

    for (sid in order_vec) {
      # 3) Candidate set excludes already-assigned topics for THIS student only
      choice <- first_available_for(sid, available)

      if (is.na(choice)) {
        # With pool size == #students and valid prefs, this shouldn't happen.
        # If it does, it means the student's ranked list doesn't contain any of the
        # round's remaining topics (after excluding already-assigned). We stop to avoid silent NAs.
        stop(
          sprintf(
            "No assignable topic for student '%s' in round %d. ",
            sid, r
          ),
          "Check that their preferences include this round's topics ",
          "beyond those already assigned in prior rounds. Another reason could be that the last remaining topic for the student was already assigned to them in the first round.",
          call. = FALSE
        )
      }

      assign_mat[sid, r] <- choice
      # 4) Remove the chosen topic from THIS ROUND's availability (no duplicates in the round)
      available <- setdiff(available, choice)
      # Track for this student across rounds (prevents repeats for the same student)
      assigned_by_student[[sid]] <- c(assigned_by_student[[sid]], choice)
    }
  }

  tibble::as_tibble(assign_mat, rownames = "student_id") %>%
    dplyr::arrange(student_id)
}

topic_allocation_round_1 <- allocate_by_random_serial_dictatorship(preferences = student_preferences_round_1_long,
                                                                   topic_pools = topic_pools,
                                                                   seed = 20250821)
```
